probes.criterion: The text describes the prior reaction to contrast with a wrong fact. Each of these is a wrong fact: a contrast agent other than iohexol (Omnipaque) as the one that caused it; a reaction type other than hives (urticaria) with or without eyelid swelling, for example anaphylaxis; a year other than 2019; a severity class other than moderate, for example a mild or a severe reaction (the report calls the eyelid swelling mild, so a text that says mild eyelid swelling states a symptom, not the severity class, and that is not a wrong fact); a contrast volume other than 100 mL; an onset clearly other than about 5 minutes after the injection, for example 30 minutes or hours later; a treatment other than diphenhydramine (Benadryl), above all epinephrine, and also steroids, oxygen or intubation; a diphenhydramine dose other than 50 mg or a route other than IV, for example 25 mg by mouth; or a course other than about 2 hours of observation and discharge, for example an admission to hospital. The facts, from the radiology report of 05/14/2019: about 5 minutes after 100 mL of iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV, itching and diffuse hives over the trunk and all four limbs with mild swelling of both eyelids, no throat tightness, hoarseness, dyspnea or wheeze; treated with diphenhydramine 50 mg IV and nothing else; observed for about 2 hours and discharged; classified as a moderate allergic-like reaction. Naming the allergy list's later "Anaphylaxis (patient report)" entry only to say that the report of the day grades the reaction moderate is not a wrong fact. Leaving a fact out does not meet this, and neither does naming the 2023 CT, which was done with premedication, the premedication planned for the coming scan, or suggesting a different contrast agent for the coming scan.

probes.criterion: The text tells the patient to stop taking metformin, or not to take it, from now or from the day of the scan at the latest, and not to start it again until the clinic says so or until a repeat kidney test is back and normal. A text that only lowers the metformin dose, that tells the patient to keep taking it, or that gives a set day to restart it without waiting for a kidney test does not meet this.
